preamble: Word-final nasal /ẽ/ (from earlier vowel + nasal coda) developed a palatal off-glide in Portuguese, giving the nasal diphthong [ẽj̃] in Brazil and [ɐ̃j̃] in European Portuguese (bem, tem, vem, também). The outcome is nasalized; the atlas has no nasal-diphthong symbol, so this cell is the closest available. Galician, which shares the medieval forms (ben), did not diphthongize. No well-documented parallel outside Portuguese has been found.

examples.note: Final nasal ẽ acquires a nasalized palatal glide; European Portuguese additionally centralizes the nucleus.
Same development in the verb form; Galician keeps vén without a glide.

sources: Wiktionary (2026). bem (Portuguese; < Old Galician-Portuguese ben < Latin bene). https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/bem
